issue_context.title: Change the name of metrics in scheduler perf-tests
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

We have `defaultMetricsCollectorConfig` here with unit as `seconds`
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b4b2345f9a4faa08715a1bf3114e6312938f8736/test/integration/scheduler_perf/scheduler_perf_test.go#L86-L96

But actually the unit is `ms`, see here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b4b2345f9a4faa08715a1bf3114e6312938f8736/test/integration/scheduler_perf/util.go#L275-L285

Proposed to change this like `scheduler_framework_extension_point_duration_seconds` -> `scheduler_framework_extension_point_duration` to avoid confusing, but have no idea this is intended or will break the dashboard. 
/cc @marseel 

/kind cleanup
/sig scheduling

### What did you expect to happen?

Better naming with no confusion.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

N/A

@kerthcet I would like to take this up.

/assign
This is still waiting for confirmation, cc @mars1024 Would you mind to give a direction, will this break the perf-test dashboard by changing the metric label values.
shouldn't the name match the one we have defined in the scheduler, which is `framework_extension_point_duration_seconds`, otherwise we will not be able to look it up.

Oh yes... got messed up. By the way, maybe we can make the name `scheduler_framework_extension_point_duration_seconds` a combined name, like `SchedulerSubsystem + schedulingLatencyName`, better to display where it came from and avoid wrong spellings.

What we want to is : 

in /pkg/scheduler/metrics/metric.go:
```
var SchedulingAttemptDurationSeconds = "scheduling_attempt_duration_seconds"
```

in /test/integration/scheduler_perf/scheduler_perf_test.go:
```
"scheduler_framework_extension_point_duration_seconds" -> metrics.SchedulerSubsystem + "_" + metrics.SchedulingAttemptDurationSeconds
```

@kerthcet Is this change, good to go, I think we should create one variable for ```metrics.SchedulerSubsystem + "_" + metrics.SchedulingAttemptDurationSeconds```. should store in one variable something like: **`schedulerSubsystemAttemptDurationSeconds`**
I think we can go ahead with this. Also the `Filter` and `Score` extension point label.

Displaying scheduler_perf data in perf-dash is currently broken and needs quite a bit more thought and experiments to fix it. This goes beyond renaming one metric, but perhaps we can use this issue for tracking the problem? I can also create a new issue, but then the solution for that would conflict with a PR for this one here.

Only `scheduler_framework_extension_point_duration_seconds` works. Even then, some workloads don't seem to have data for "Score", so only "Filter" actually renders anything.

For results where there is no plugin label, for example `SchedulingThroughput`, nothing is shown because no data has "Score" or "Filter" as label value.

The conclusion [from Slack](https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C09QZTRH7/p1684856425322669?thread_ts=1676392759.560789&cid=C09QZTRH7) was that "you should not mix labels in the same file", i.e. all data items in the same file must have the same labels. We also have to be careful to avoid label combinations with no data.

Another suggestion from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118202/commits/62844bc4c1171b584d1032aa760ae78cbaca2749#r1234780609 that needs be discussed: adding a prefix to `runtime_seconds`.
@nikzayn: do you intend to continue working on this, considering that it is not as simple as just renaming some strings?
@pohly I will do this, I know that string manipulation is not the only thing but one should explain everything in the ticket description adequately.

I cannot update the ticket description, and the desired solution is unknown at this time. See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/116204#issuecomment-1563895137 for a description of the problem. If this is too vague for you, then let someone else work on this.

I don't think it makes sense to merge https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/116735 while we have a much bigger problem.

Yes please someone else work on this.

/unassign
